newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Command expects increase in Ravva oil.
newsitem.headline: Command expects increase in Ravva oil.

text.p: Oil producer Command Petroleum Ltd said on Friday that its RC-2 well in the Ravva contract area, offshore India, had encountered a substantial oil column with the result expected to lead to an as-yet unquantified increase in the Ravva's field oil reserves.

Command said the well, drilled with the primary purpose of being a down flank water-injection well, had intersected the top of the main field reservoir about 35 metres high to pre-drill prognosis. The well intersected an interpreted 48 metre gross oil column of which 45.2 metres was net oil pay in good quality reservoir sands, Command said.

Participating interests in the Ravva Contract Area are operator Command with 22.5 percent, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation 40 percent, Videocon Petroleum Ltd 25 percent and Marubeni Corporation with 12.5 percent.
Command is currently in a merger process with British oil producer Cairn Energy Plc.
Cairn is offering a choice of a A$1.10 a share cash offer or a scrip offer of two Cairn shares for every 13 Command shares.
By 1.55 p.m. (0355 GMT), Command shares were down a cent at A$1.13 on turnover of 738,989 shares.
